_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: project_mcp_sync_envvar_and_promote_toolsmanifest.md (reprint 2026-06-06, press 4.22.0, Level RMM).

handfixes.summary: Auth env var stays the spec canonical LEVEL_API_TOKEN everywhere; mcp-sync/promote rewrite it to the slug-derived LEVELIO_API_TOKEN, breaking MCP auth
handfixes.why: Level's spec x-auth-env-vars is LEVEL_API_TOKEN (not LEVELIO_*). config.go reads LEVEL_API_TOKEN, but press 4.22.0 `mcp-sync` derives the var from the api_name slug and rewrites manifest.json (user_config + mcp_config.env), .printing-press.json, tools.go agent hints, and tools-manifest.json to LEVELIO_API_TOKEN while config.go keeps the canonical - a silent 401 for every .mcpb/MCP user. `lock promote` re-triggers it. A reprint/polish/promote plants the bug again. The fix keeps LEVEL_API_TOKEN aligned across config.go + manifest + server + tools.go.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Fix belongs in the press: mcp-sync must honor x-auth-env-vars and never derive the auth var from the api_name slug. Filed as a retro (manuscripts/levelio/20260606-173908 findings).

handfixes.summary: `levelio-mcp` accepts --transport/--addr and PP_MCP_TRANSPORT, matching the 58 connectors that already do
handfixes.why: main() called server.ServeStdio unconditionally and never parsed os.Args, so `levelio-mcp --transport http` was silently ignored and the process still served stdio. Four of the six affected connectors ship an mcp-install.md instructing users to pass exactly that flag, so the documentation described a mode the binary did not have. The block added here is copied verbatim from the generated shape the other 58 connectors already carry (see skills/halopsa/cli/cmd/halopsa-mcp/main.go): a --transport flag defaulting to defaultTransport(), which reads PP_MCP_TRANSPORT and falls back to stdio so no-argument invocation is unchanged, an --addr flag defaulting to :7777, and a switch that serves stdio, serves NewStreamableHTTPServer for http, or exits 2 on an unknown value. This is press drift rather than staleness: cork and avanan are on a NEWER press than several connectors that already have the flag, so a reprint at the current press will not reliably restore it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Make the transport flag block unconditional in the cli-printing-press MCP main template so every future print carries it, and add a generator check that fails when an mcp-install.md documents a flag the printed main.go does not parse (filed as a retro item against the generator).
